title: An MI300X Over MCP: What the Matrix Cores Execute, and What They Don't
why_read: A hands-on hardware benchmarking piece measuring real numeric-format performance on an AMD MI300X GPU offers concrete, verified data that corrects vendor spec sheets.
analysis: The author built a set of MCP-based Python tools to remotely manage and benchmark a rented AMD Instinct MI300X GPU, measuring real throughput for fp8, int8, and fp4 formats directly from the hardware rather than trusting AMD's published numbers. Notably, they found fp8 e4m3fnuz runs 1.77x faster than bf16, int8 runs slower at 0.69x despite AMD rating it the same as fp8, and fp4 isn't supported on this chip at all. This kind of empirical hardware verification is valuable for ML engineers making GPU purchasing or deployment decisions, since it catches discrepancies between spec sheets and actual behavior.
